supporting_evidence.quote: Google Search & other revenues increased $9.1 billion and $18.8 billion from the three and six months ended June 30, 2025 to the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. The overall growth was driven by interrelated factors including increases in search queries resulting from growth in user adoption and usage on mobile devices; growth in advertiser spending; and improvements we have made in ad formats and delivery.
Three Months Ended Six Months Ended June 30, 2026 June 30, 2026 Google Search & other Paid clicks change 13 % 13 % Cost-per-click change 3 % 4 %

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that growth in Google Search & other revenues in Q2 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) was primarily due to an increase in paid clicks. This is an interpretive/causal claim about what drove the revenue growth.

Evidence E6 confirms that Google Search & other revenues increased $9.1 billion in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and states "The overall growth was driven by interrelated factors including increases in search queries resulting from growth in user adoption and usage on mobile devices; growth in advertiser spending; and improvements we have made in ad formats and delivery."

Evidence E1 provides the monetization metrics showing that paid clicks increased 13% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, while cost-per-click increased only 3%.

The filing explicitly identifies multiple interrelated factors driving the growth, with increases in search queries (which directly relate to paid clicks) listed first among the factors. The 13% increase in paid clicks combined with only a 3% increase in cost-per-click suggests that the volume of clicks (paid clicks) was indeed a primary driver of the revenue growth. The filing's statement that growth was driven by "increases in search queries" and the substantial 13% paid clicks increase support the claim that paid clicks were a primary driver.

The claim is supported by the evidence.
